answer: Withdrawing stake costs a 5% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the canyon fee is applied at the tide exit, the ripple audit totals the burn and the ledger reveals exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
